action_summary: Counts what a weight-space learning layer would actually have to eat, instead of assuming it. The owner's analysis that token-space is one layer and weight-space is the other is correct, and its four 2026 citations check out. What it does not say is that the precondition is a verified event stream, not an update mechanism. Measured: execution receipts carry 0 usable events, the hand-seeded store 66 events and 0 verified, and the controller checkpoints 192 work steps with 64 verified and an 8.9 percent real failure rate -- a natural label split, thin and narrow. 258 units against a 5000 threshold, while 2790 changed lines per merge are discarded. Adds no capability, trains nothing, claims no benchmark movement.

measured_effect: Fuel gauge, all counted from the tree: execution receipts 305 records / 0 units (a receipt holds no situation and no choice); hand-seeded trajectory store 24 records / 66 units / 0 verified / outcomes {success}; taught-action corpora 0 stores with changes; controller checkpoints 449 files / 320 steps / 192 work steps after excluding 128 terminal `finish` steps / 64 verified / 175 passed / 17 failed = 8.9 percent real failure rate / 20 distinct capabilities / 87 distinct situations. Totals: 258 units, 64 verified, threshold 5000, ready_to_train False. Production rate: 2790 changed lines per merge over 30 merges. Two of the gauge's own first versions were wrong and both are pinned: it never opened the only file kind with an event stream, and it counted terminal steps as failures (45 percent instead of 8.9). 9 tests pass.
